name: kero
description: A cross-platform native terminal app optimized for agents
readmeExcerpt:
# Kero

A terminal for coding agents, on macOS, Windows and Linux.

Run Claude Code, Codex, a dev server or a test watcher each in its own session. Kero groups sessions by project in a sidebar that shows which are working, which need you and which are done.

- **Sessions outlive the window.** They run in `kerod`, a small daemon, so quitting Kero leaves them running. Reopen it and every pane and its scrollback is back.
- **Status at a glance.** Each pane is working, waiting, idle, error or exited. <kbd>⌘</kbd> <kbd>J</kbd> jumps to the one that needs you, and Kero notifies you when an agent finishes, fails or is blocked.
- **A CLI agents can drive.** `kero` starts sessions, splits panes, types into them, waits on them and reads their screens.
- **Remote hosts.** Run agents on a Linux box, a cloud VM, a Mac, a Windows PC or WSL and see them in the same sidebar, over SSH or Tailscale. They keep running when your laptop sleeps. See [Remote Hosts](docs/remote.md).
- **Ghostty under the hood.** Terminals render with libghostty, so Ghostty themes, fonts and config keys just work.

## Install

Download Kero from the [releases page](https://github.com/egoist/kero/releases), then choose **Kero › Install Command Line Tool…** to put `kero` on your `PATH`.

```sh
kero new -n fix-login -- claude
```

To run sessions on a Linux server, a Mac or a Windows PC, install the server build there, then add the machine in **Settings › Hosts**:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://github.com/egoist/kero/releases/latest/download/install-server.sh | sh
```

On Windows, in PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://github.com/egoist/kero/releases/latest/download/install-server.ps1 | iex
```

See the [docs](docs/index.md) for more.

## Prior art

- [**Rex**](https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/installation): Mitchell Hashimoto's terminal and multiplexer in one native app, with sessions that persist through a server and a scriptable CLI.
- [**Herdr**](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr): a terminal multiplexer for running many coding agents in one terminal, with agent status detection.

## License

MIT

releases.body:
## What's Changed
* Tell when an agent finishes in the selected session while Kero is in the background on Windows by @egoist in https://github.com/egoist/kero/pull/259
* fix(dialog): focus the confirmation action for Return by @iamvicliu in https://github.com/egoist/kero/pull/260
* Drop down a quick terminal with a global shortcut by @egoist in https://github.com/egoist/kero/pull/257

## New Contributors
* @iamvicliu made their first contribution in https://github.com/egoist/kero/pull/260

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/egoist/kero/compare/v2.1.19...v2.1.20

releases.name: v2.1.19
releases.body:
## What's Changed
* Stop Windows CJK from falling back to proportional YaHei by @egoist in https://github.com/egoist/kero/pull/251
* Run a session in its own git worktree by @egoist in https://github.com/egoist/kero/pull/254
* Open projects by dropping folders into the sidebar by @p1xelll in https://github.com/egoist/kero/pull/212
* Resume agents' past conversations from the palette, the sidebar and the CLI by @egoist in https://github.com/egoist/kero/pull/253
* Move the window by dragging the sidebar's empty space by @egoist in https://github.com/egoist/kero/pull/255

## New Contributors
* @p1xelll made their first contribution in https://github.com/egoist/kero/pull/212

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/egoist/kero/compare/v2.1.18...v2.1.19

releases.name: v2.1.18
releases.body:
## What's Changed
* Let programs run in Kero ask for the microphone, the camera and other apps by @egoist in https://github.com/egoist/kero/pull/244
* Add a copy button beside the download page install commands by @egoist in https://github.com/egoist/kero/pull/245
* Reach SSH hosts with the agent the login shell sets, as 1Password's by @egoist in https://github.com/egoist/kero/pull/247
* Add Close All Sessions to a project's context menu by @egoist in https://github.com/egoist/kero/pull/250


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/egoist/kero/compare/v2.1.17...v2.1.18

releases.name: v2.1.17
releases.body:
## What's Changed
* Update MyGo, so macOS 27 no longer runs an AutoFill helper for Kero by @egoist in https://github.com/egoist/kero/pull/234
* Tell Codex panes their sessions when Codex's app server runs their hooks by @egoist in https://github.com/egoist/kero/pull/238
* Browser: accessibility snapshot with refs, unshown screenshots, cookie save/load by @egoist in https://github.com/egoist/kero/pull/242


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/egoist/kero/compare/v2.1.16...v2.1.17

aiSummary.oneLiner: A native, Swift-based terminal workspace for macOS featuring integrated file trees, split panes, and project grouping.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Kero is a highly polished, native macOS terminal emulator built with Swift and powered by the libghostty engine, offering a modern workspace alternative to traditional command lines. It provides a highly structured environment that natively supports project-based organization, visual file trees, and fluid split panes without requiring heavy configuration files like tmux. It can also utilize an Alacritty backend optionally. The design aggressively focuses on bringing a native, deeply integrated GUI experience to terminal-heavy workflows, aligning perfectly with modern macOS UX paradigms. It significantly reduces the cognitive friction of managing multiple complex terminal sessions.
keyFeatures: Native macOS UI: Built meticulously with Swift for superior performance and deep visual integration with the operating system's design language.
libghostty Engine: Uses the exceptionally fast and robust ghostty terminal engine by default for accurate text rendering and command processing.
Project Grouping: Intelligently organizes terminal sessions by project directories, keeping context strictly isolated and easily accessible via tabs.
Integrated File Tree: Includes a visual, interactive sidebar to browse project files directly next to the active terminal pane.
Split Panes: Native, intuitive support for dividing the workspace into multiple terminal views without relying on complex external multiplexers.

useCases.title: Context Switching
useCases.description: Developers working concurrently across multiple microservices can group their terminal tabs by project to maintain strict organization.

useCases.title: Integrated Workflow
useCases.description: Users who prefer having a visual file explorer immediately alongside their command line operations without launching a full IDE.

useCases.title: Native Experience
useCases.description: macOS power users seeking a fast terminal that feels like a native application rather than a sluggish cross-platform Electron wrapper.

useCases.title: Multiplexer Replacement
useCases.description: Developers who desperately want split panes and session management out-of-the-box without spending hours configuring tmux.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: macOS software developers and system administrators who spend a significant portion of their day in the terminal and desire a native workspace.
